input.strategy_title: Default Vector Store for Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag
input.strategy_markdown:
## Summary

RHOAI must provide a default vector store that is available out-of-the-box — without manual setup — so that Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag continue to function when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution image. Today these capabilities depend on an inline vector store provider bundled within the Llama Stack process; removing it (per RHAISTRAT-7474) will break them unless an alternative is available at the platform level.

## Problem Statement

Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag currently rely on an inline Milvus provider embedded in the Llama Stack distribution image to store and retrieve vector embeddings. This inline provider runs inside the Llama Stack process itself.

RHAISTRAT-7474 proposes removing inline providers from the Llama Stack distribution to improve GA readiness — shipping only what can be tested and maintained at scale, and aligning with Llama Stack's primary use case as a remote API server. However, no platform-level alternative exists today. If inline providers are removed without a replacement, any RHOAI user relying on Gen AI Studio's RAG capabilities or Auto Rag will lose functionality entirely — there is no workaround short of manually provisioning and configuring an external vector database.

Users expect vector storage to "just work" when they use Gen AI Studio or Auto Rag. The current out-of-the-box experience must be preserved even as the underlying architecture evolves.

## Affected Customers

* All RHOAI customers using Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities
* All RHOAI customers using Auto Rag
* This is a platform-level product dependency: these features cannot function without a vector store

## Business Justification

* **Product integrity:** Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag are GA-track capabilities in RHOAI. Removing the inline vector store without a replacement breaks shipped product functionality for every user of these features.
* **Blocking dependency:** RHAISTRAT-7474 (removing inline providers for GA readiness) cannot proceed until this RFE is resolved. Silas Brenmark (Gen AI Studio lead) has identified this as a blocker.
* **User experience:** RHOAI differentiates on integrated, opinionated defaults. Requiring users to manually provision and configure a vector database before they can use the playground or Auto Rag degrades the out-of-the-box experience that customers expect from the platform.

## Acceptance Criteria

* \[ \] A default vector store is available out-of-the-box on RHOAI without requiring users to manually provision or configure external infrastructure
* \[ \] Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] Auto Rag functions with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] The default vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the Llama Stack instance (not an inline provider)
* \[ \] The default vector store is scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments (e.g., per-namespace isolation)
* \[ \] The default vector store is lightweight enough to run in resource-constrained environments without imposing significant overhead

## Success Criteria

* Users of Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag experience no functional regression when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution
* No additional manual setup steps are required for RAG workflows compared to the current experience
* RHAISTRAT-7474 is unblocked and can proceed to implementation

## Open Questions

* What is the preferred scoping model — per namespace, per Llama Stack instance, or both? (Silas noted per-namespace is preferred for isolation, but Auto Rag may need per-instance scoping)
* Should users have a migration path from the default vector store to a production-grade vector database? (Bram Sundqvist raised the importance of aligning with commonly-used vector DB providers for easier migration)

## Strategy (AI Generated by Agentic SDLC Pipeline)

> **Note:** The full strategy exceeds Jira's description size limit and is stored as an attachment: `RHAISTRAT-8004-strategy.md`.

## Staff Engineer Input

**Correction 1 — OGX does not auto-provision PostgreSQL.** OGX defaults to SQLite for storage (`storage.kv.type: sqlite`, `storage.sql.type: sqlite` in the OGXServer CRD). The odh-dashboard gen-ai BFF hardcodes SQLite when creating OGXServer instances for the playground (`kv_sqlite` and `sql_sqlite` in `llamastack_config.go`). PostgreSQL is a supported backend but must be user-configured with an explicit `connectionString` secret. The strategy's claim that "every LlamaStackDistribution instance requires a PostgreSQL database" is incorrect — introducing PostgreSQL is new work, not an extension of existing infrastructure.

**Correction 2 — A Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector already exists.** The `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16` image includes pgvector out of the box — confirmed in the [sclorg/postgresql-container Dockerfile](https://github.com/sclorg/postgresql-container/blob/master/16/Dockerfile.rhel9) (`INSTALL_PKGS="$INSTALL_PKGS pgvector"`). PostgreSQL 18 (RHEL 9) also includes pgvector. Furthermore, the model-registry-operator already uses `postgresql-16` as its auto-provisioned database image, and `RELATED_IMAGE_POSTGRESQL_16_IMAGE` is already present in the rhods-operator CSV for disconnected installs. No custom image build is needed. No Konflux onboarding is needed. The 1-2 sprint image onboarding estimate in the strategy can be eliminated.

**Architectural direction — platform-level database vs. self-provisioned.** Multiple RHOAI components now need PostgreSQL (model-registry, MLflow, and now OGX for pgvector). The preferred long-term direction is a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL managed via the DSC, where each component consumes a connection string rather than self-provisioning. A shared platform-provided PostgreSQL via DSC will not be available until RHOAI 3.6. For 3.5, Gen AI Studio must provision its own PostgreSQL instance.

**Operator dependency for self-provisioning (RHAISTRAT-7164).** Self-provisioning PostgreSQL following the model-registry-operator pattern requires a RHOAI-controlled operator for Gen AI Studio. The ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic. The dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) would provide this operator layer. This is a hard dependency — until RHAISTRAT-7164 delivers, there is no RHOAI-controlled operator where PostgreSQL lifecycle management can live. It will be challenging to commit this strategy to a specific release until that dependency is delivered.

**Fallback if RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time.** If the dashboard modularization is not ready for 3.5, the fallback is to require customers to bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the Playground. Users would manually configure the OGXServer CR spec with their PostgreSQL connection details. This aligns with the breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0, even though the Playground largely abstracts OGX from users. The development team should define a go/no-go gate for this decision as part of sprint planning.

**Decouple from Auto Rag.** Auto Rag integration with Gen AI Studio (RHAISTRAT-7824) is targeting RHOAI 3.6. This strategy should validate pgvector only for Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows. Auto Rag compatibility with pgvector will be addressed in RHAISTRAT-7824's scope. Remove Auto Rag from affected components, impacted teams, acceptance criteria, and validation requirements.

**Performance and index thresholds — dev experimentation scope.** The default pgvector instance is meant for development experimentation, not production usage. Strict latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99) are not required. The sprint 1 benchmark should capture the inline Milvus baseline and verify pgvector is in the same order of magnitude, not meet a specific threshold. Typical Playground RAG usage involves small document sets — flat scan (no index) is sufficient for the default. Users with production-scale vector workloads should use an external vector database. Remove open questions about latency thresholds, corpus size ranges, and index type selection.

**PostgreSQL resource sizing.** Reference the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource requests/limits as the starting point. Adjust based on sprint 1 benchmarking if needed.

**Alternative fallback — BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning.** If RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time, an alternative to requiring customers to bring their own PostgreSQL is to have the gen-ai BFF provision the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly, similar to how the BFF currently provisions guardrails infrastructure. The BFF would create the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret when a playground with RAG is configured, if one does not already exist in the namespace. Caveats: (1) the implementation must be designed for portability — when the platform-provided shared database becomes available (3.6), the BFF should consume the shared connection string rather than self-provisioning; (2) lifecycle management of the PostgreSQL instance must be carefully considered — the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion, handling of pod restarts, and credential rotation need explicit design attention.

**Existing remote vector store implementation is reusable.** Per the engineering team, the existing remote vector store implementation can be largely reused for pgvector integration. The majority of the work effort is around infrastructure and provisioning of the PostgreSQL/pgvector database, not the vector_io provider integration itself.

**Correction 3 — Vector storage and application storage are independent configurations.** The OGX vector_io provider configuration (`remote::pgvector` via `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) is completely separate from OGX's application storage backend configuration (`storage.kv.type`, `storage.sql.type`). This strategy only needs to configure the pgvector vector_io provider — it does not change the application storage backend, which remains on its existing default (SQLite). There is no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration concern because the application storage is not being touched. Remove any references to consolidating vector and application storage in a single database, and remove any SQLite-to-PostgreSQL upgrade path considerations.

# Operator-Based PostgreSQL/pgvector Provisioning for Gen AI Studio (Go Outcome)

## Description

Branch outcome "go": the dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164) delivers the
RHOAI-controlled operator layer in time for the target release, and PostgreSQL/pgvector lifecycle
management for Gen AI Studio playgrounds is implemented in that operator following the
model-registry-operator's auto-provisioning pattern. The operator provisions a PostgreSQL instance
(using the existing Red Hat `rhel9/postgresql-16` image, which includes pgvector out of the box —
no custom image build) scoped per the confirmed scoping model (per-namespace by default), and
exposes the connection secret that the playground OGXServer wiring consumes. This branch exists
only if the go/no-go decision selects the operator-based approach; the decision's external
precondition is that RHAISTRAT-7164 actually delivers the operator layer.

## Scope

- Implement PostgreSQL/pgvector instance lifecycle management in the RHOAI-controlled operator
  layer delivered by the dashboard operator modularization, following the model-registry-operator
  pattern for auto-provisioned databases (Deployment, Service, credentials secret, and related
  resources).
- Use the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector; wire the image reference for
  disconnected installs following the existing related-image environment variable pattern already
  present in the platform operator CSV.
- Scope provisioned instances per the confirmed scoping model (per-namespace isolation by
  default).
- Expose the PostgreSQL connection secret in the playground namespace, satisfying the
  connection-secret contract consumed by the playground OGXServer vector_io wiring.
- Set resource requests/limits starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL reference
  values, adjusted per benchmark findings.
- Handle lifecycle: provisioning on demand, and cleanup/garbage collection when the playground
  (or its namespace) is removed.
- Document the provisioning behavior for inclusion in the user-facing documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Gen AI Studio playground with RAG enabled gets a working PostgreSQL/pgvector instance
  provisioned automatically, with no manual user setup, in a cluster with the operator installed.
- The provisioned instance uses the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector (no custom
  image build, no new pipeline onboarding).
- The connection secret satisfies the contract consumed by the playground OGXServer vector_io
  wiring, and playground RAG works end-to-end against the provisioned instance.
- Instances are scoped per the confirmed scoping model (per-namespace isolation by default) —
  tenants in different namespaces do not share vector data.
- Resource requests/limits start from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL reference values
  and are recorded with rationale (benchmark-adjusted where available).
- Provisioned resources are cleaned up when the playground is deleted.
- Disconnected-install support: the PostgreSQL image reference is resolvable via the
  related-image environment variable pattern.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box, no manual provisioning).
- AC-2 (playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store) — provisioning completes
  the end-to-end path.
- AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping, per-namespace isolation).
- AC-6 (lightweight for resource-constrained environments) — resource sizing.
- SE-1 (model-registry-operator auto-provisioning pattern, no custom image).
- SE-6 (no additional manual setup steps).
- SE-8 (resource sizing from model-registry-operator reference).

# BFF-Managed PostgreSQL/pgvector Provisioning for Gen AI Studio Playgrounds (No-Go Outcome)

## Description

Branch outcome "no-go": the dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164) does not deliver
the RHOAI-controlled operator layer in time for the target release, and the go/no-go decision
selects BFF-managed provisioning as the fallback. The gen-ai BFF provisions the
PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly when a playground with RAG is configured and no suitable
PostgreSQL connection already exists in the namespace — the same pattern the BFF already uses to
provision guardrails infrastructure. The BFF creates the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and
Secret using the existing Red Hat `rhel9/postgresql-16` image (which includes pgvector out of the
box — no custom image build). Because the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, the
lifecycle caveats flagged by the Staff Engineer Input (cleanup on playground deletion, pod
restart handling, credential rotation) require explicit design attention in this epic.

## Scope

- Implement BFF-managed provisioning of a PostgreSQL/pgvector instance (Deployment, Service,
  PVC, credentials Secret) when a playground with RAG is configured and no PostgreSQL connection
  secret satisfying the wiring contract already exists in the namespace.
- Use the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector; no custom image build.
- Design for portability: when the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL becomes available (planned
  RHOAI 3.6), the BFF consumes the shared connection string instead of self-provisioning — the
  provisioning path must be cleanly replaceable by configuration.
- Explicitly design and handle lifecycle management without a reconciliation loop:
  - cleanup of provisioned resources when the playground is deleted;
  - behavior on BFF pod restarts (idempotent reconciliation of expected resources);
  - credential handling and any rotation strategy.
- Scope provisioned instances per-namespace (the playground's namespace), matching the confirmed
  scoping model.
- Set resource requests/limits starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL reference
  values, adjusted per benchmark findings.
- Document the provisioning behavior and its limits for inclusion in the user-facing
  documentation.
- If, during design, the lifecycle caveats prove unviable, escalate back through the go/no-go
  decision to the bring-your-own posture (user-configured PostgreSQL via the OGXServer CR spec,
  covered by the wiring work and documentation rather than auto-provisioning).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Gen AI Studio playground with RAG enabled gets a working PostgreSQL/pgvector instance
  provisioned automatically by the BFF, with no manual user setup, when no user-supplied
  PostgreSQL configuration exists.
- The provisioned instance uses the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector (no custom
  image build).
- The connection secret satisfies the contract consumed by the playground OGXServer vector_io
  wiring, and playground RAG works end-to-end against the provisioned instance.
- Provisioned resources are cleaned up when the playground is deleted; BFF pod restarts do not
  cause duplicate or broken PostgreSQL resources (idempotent handling is demonstrated).
- Credential handling (creation and any rotation approach) is designed and documented.
- The provisioning path is replaceable by a shared connection string with configuration changes
  only (portability demonstrated or validated by design review).
- Instances are scoped per-namespace — tenants in different namespaces do not share vector data.
- Resource requests/limits start from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL reference values
  and are recorded with rationale (benchmark-adjusted where available).

## HLR Traceability

- AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box, no manual provisioning).
- AC-2 (playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store) — provisioning completes
  the end-to-end path.
- AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping, per-namespace isolation).
- AC-6 (lightweight for resource-constrained environments) — resource sizing.
- SE-4 (portability to the platform-provided shared connection string in RHOAI 3.6).
- SE-6 (no additional manual setup steps).
- SE-8 (resource sizing from model-registry-operator reference).

# Default Vector Store Provisioning Approach Go/No-Go Decision

## Description

This investigation resolves the single largest uncertainty in the default vector store strategy:
how the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance for Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows gets provisioned
for the target release. The Staff Engineer Input established that operator-based self-provisioning
(following the model-registry-operator pattern) requires a RHOAI-controlled operator layer that
only the dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) can provide, and that this
is a hard dependency with uncertain timing. If that dependency does not land in time, the fallback
options are BFF-managed provisioning (the gen-ai BFF creates the PostgreSQL resources directly,
as it already does for guardrails infrastructure) or requiring customers to bring their own
PostgreSQL. The Staff Engineer Input directs the development team to define a go/no-go gate for
this decision as part of sprint planning.

## Scope

- Define explicit go/no-go criteria and a decision date for whether the dashboard operator
  modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164) will deliver the RHOAI-controlled operator layer in time for the
  target release (RHOAI 3.5).
- Track RHAISTRAT-7164 delivery status and confidence against those criteria.
- If the outcome is "no-go": decide between BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning and a
  bring-your-own-PostgreSQL posture, evaluating the BFF-managed approach's known caveats
  (lifecycle management without a reconciliation loop: cleanup on playground deletion, pod
  restart handling, credential rotation, and portability to the platform-provided shared
  PostgreSQL planned for RHOAI 3.6).
- Confirm the scoping model for the default vector store (per-namespace vs per-OGXServer-instance).
  Per-namespace is the working direction per the component lead's preference for isolation; the
  main per-instance driver (Auto Rag) has been decoupled from this strategy.
- Record the outcome as a decision record (selected provisioning mechanism, scoping model, and
  rationale) that selects the downstream provisioning implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Go/no-go criteria and a decision date for the RHAISTRAT-7164 dependency are documented and
  agreed in sprint planning before the decision is made.
- A decision record exists that selects exactly one provisioning approach (operator-based,
  BFF-managed, or bring-your-own) with rationale grounded in RHAISTRAT-7164's actual delivery
  status.
- The scoping model (per-namespace or per-instance) is confirmed in the same decision record.
- The decision is socialized with the Gen AI Studio lead and the engineering team, and the
  selected downstream provisioning work is unblocked (or explicitly descoped to a
  bring-your-own posture with documentation).

## HLR Traceability

- AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping, e.g. per-namespace isolation) — scoping model confirmation.
- SE-1 / SE-2 (provisioning pattern selection and bring-your-own fallback) — go/no-go decision.
- SE-6 (no additional manual setup steps) — the decision determines whether manual setup can be
  avoided entirely.

# Benchmark pgvector Against the Inline Milvus Baseline for Playground RAG and Recommend Resource Sizing

## Description

Validate that pgvector is an acceptable default vector store for Gen AI Studio playground RAG
workloads in dev-experimentation scope, and produce the resource-sizing recommendation for the
default PostgreSQL/pgvector instance. Per the Staff Engineer Input, strict latency SLAs are not
required: the benchmark captures the inline Milvus baseline (before it is removed from the
distribution) and verifies pgvector performs in the same order of magnitude on representative
playground workloads. Typical playground usage involves small document sets, for which flat scan
(no index) is expected to be sufficient. This is a Tier 1 risk-reduction validation that runs in
parallel with the implementation work; its sizing output feeds the provisioning implementations
as tuning input (they start from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource
requests/limits as the reference).

## Scope

- Build a repeatable benchmark harness for representative playground RAG operations (document
  ingestion and similarity search over small document sets) exercised through the OGX vector I/O
  API.
- Capture the inline Milvus provider baseline on the same workload before inline providers are
  removed from the distribution.
- Run the same workload against a PostgreSQL/pgvector backend (flat scan, no index) and compare
  order of magnitude.
- Record PostgreSQL resource consumption (CPU/memory) under the benchmark workload and recommend
  resource requests/limits, using the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource
  requests/limits as the starting reference.
- Document results and a go/no-go-style assessment: is pgvector acceptable as the
  dev-experimentation default, or does the gap warrant revisiting the default-store choice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The inline Milvus baseline is captured on the representative workload and recorded before
  inline provider removal.
- pgvector results on the same workload are recorded and compared; pgvector is within the same
  order of magnitude as the baseline for playground-scale document sets (no specific latency
  threshold applies — dev-experimentation scope).
- A resource-sizing recommendation for the default PostgreSQL/pgvector instance is produced,
  starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL requests/limits and adjusted based on
  the measured consumption.
- Benchmark harness and results are documented well enough to be re-run when sizing needs
  revisiting.
- Users with production-scale vector workloads are noted as out of scope for the default store
  (they should use an external vector database) — recorded in the findings.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-2 (no loss of current capability) — measurement basis for the no-regression claim.
- AC-6 (lightweight enough for resource-constrained environments) — sizing recommendation.
- SE-7 (order-of-magnitude benchmark, flat scan acceptable, no strict SLAs).
- SE-8 (resource sizing from model-registry-operator reference, adjusted per benchmark).
